items.detail: All three sub-parts verified by running the tests. (1) Extraction test: tests/test_xml_specs.py:1508-1519 documented_migration_example() regex-extracts the fenced ```xml block carrying id="REQ-MIG-1" from docs/XML-SPEC-SCHEMA.md (asserts exactly one such block); resolving_example() (:1521-1531) substitutes the four illustrative path literals via DOCUMENTED_PATHS (:1492-1503); test_the_documented_migration_example_validates (:1534-1545) drives auger.main(["spec","validate",...]) in-process (run_spec at :137) and asserts rc 0 plus 'spec: 1 document(s), 2 block(s), 1 reference(s) ok'. RAN: python3 -m pytest tests/test_xml_specs.py::test_the_documented_migration_example_validates tests/test_xml_specs.py::test_a_mutual_verifies_pair_is_the_refusal_the_document_quotes -v -> '2 passed in 0.35s'. (2) Doc rule: docs/XML-SPEC-SCHEMA.md (paragraph above the example) states 'The `verifies` edge is declared on ONE side of a pair ... declaring both for the same pair is a cycle, refused as `spec error (reference-cycle): REQ-MIG-1 -> TEST-MIG-1 -> REQ-MIG-1` (rc 2)' — one sentence covering both halves with the refusal text quoted; test_a_mutual_verifies_pair_is_the_refusal_the_document_quotes (:1548-1573) asserts 'declared on ONE side' is present and that QUOTED_REFUSAL (:1505) matches exactly once. (3) Loader/cycle-detector agreement: auger.py:8606 _spec_refuse_reference_cycles walks the typed edge graph (verifies included via SPEC_EDGE_ATTRS) and raises SpecError('reference-cycle', path) at auger.py:8634; the mutual shape is pinned twice — the new test builds the mutual variant from the documented example and asserts rc 2 with the doc-quoted text appearing in stderr (so doc and code cannot drift apart without a red test), and pre-existing test_bundle_refuses_a_requirement_declaring_both_edge_directions (:871-883) pins the same refusal on the bundle path.
